evidence_chain.interpretation: The route token is directly present in allocated non-executable ELF data.
The trusted table entry route slot points to the route token address.
The same trusted entry handler slot points into an allocated executable section.

negative_controls.case: route and handler-like names exist without a profiled table entry
negative_controls.result: no binding and no deep evidence

negative_controls.case: pointer pair occurs in an untrusted .data__ section

actual_tenda_ac9.interpretation: AC9 exposes route strings and exported handler symbols but has no trusted named route-table section. The conservative profile therefore leaves its route/handler obligations open; a call-site/decompiler Adapter is required.

safety_invariants: String or symbol name similarity never closes an obligation.
The route table section name and pointer layout are part of the versioned profile.
Every handler pointer must resolve into allocated executable ELF memory.
Every published proof retains a replayable binary span and artifact digest.
